bounded_statement: The report's selected result asserts a fledging rate 'for the complete planned set of 60 nest sites' of 37.5 percent, but that figure is computed as 18 events divided by the 48 retained post-screening sites; the rate actually characterizes the retained subset (18/48 = 37.5%), not the complete planned domain of 60 units that the task and the report's own 'Scientific target' section declare (18/60 would be 30.0%). The claim's stated domain (complete planned set) and its computational domain (retained subset) demonstrably diverge within the visible files.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the full unit accounting and even states the 48-site denominator inside the selected-result sentence, so a careful reader could detect the mismatch; the disclosure argues against concealment but does not cure the domain/denominator mismatch in the headline claim.

Independent recount of inputs/data.csv confirms 60 planned rows, 12 rows with camera_uptime_pct below 80.0 (all with fledged=unknown), 48 retained, and 18 retained rows with fledged=yes, so 18/48 = 37.5% is the retained-subset rate and 18/60 = 30.0% is the planned-set confirmed-event rate.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the verdict three ways. (1) Maybe 37.5% could be read as a legitimate estimate for the complete planned set under a missing-at-random assumption for the 12 unknown-outcome sites; but the report makes no such estimation claim, states no amendment or approved deviation, and phrases the result as a computed rate 'for the complete planned set of 60 nest sites ... divided by 48 nest sites', which is a direct scope/denominator contradiction rather than a modeled estimate. (2) Maybe the disclosed 18/48 arithmetic makes the claim internally honest; the arithmetic is disclosed, but the claim's asserted domain (60 planned sites) still does not match its computational domain (48 retained sites), which is precisely the in-scope issue class. (3) I recomputed all counts from inputs/data.csv (60 planned, 12 below the 80.0 threshold split 4/4/4 across sectors, 18 'yes' among retained) and confirmed the report's numbers are faithful to the workflow — the defect is the labeling of a retained-subset rate as the complete-domain rate, not a numerical error. No falsification succeeded.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py sets `denominator = retained_units` (48) while the report template labels the resulting rate as applying to the complete planned set of `planned_units` (60), so a retained-subset proportion is presented under a complete-domain scientific target with no protocol amendment or approved deviation.
